title: We took the feedback from the last post and changed a few things
author: Open_Swimming5859
selftext:
I posted here a couple days ago asking what people would need before letting an AI trading agent touch real funds.

Got some genuinely useful feedback, and a few comments made us rethink parts of how we were approaching Agon.

The biggest one was that the agent should never be the thing deciding or changing its own limits.

So now, anything we infer from your trading history is treated more like a suggestion first. You see it, review it, and decide what actually becomes a rule.

Every trade also goes through the same guardrail check. The agent doesn’t get its own route around it.

We’re also working on things people mentioned in the last thread like hard spending caps, emergency revoke, owner-only permission changes, fail-closed execution and proper activity logs.

One thing I probably didn’t explain properly in the last post is **how we actually want people to use Agon**.

We’re building it to work directly inside your terminal / Claude Code / opencode, so you can look through markets, check a token, see your positions and limits, place trades yourself, or let the agent act when you want it to.

There is a web dashboard too, but the terminal side is a pretty big part of what we’re building.

Attaching a few screenshots of where that’s at right now.

Still early, and I’m mostly curious about this from people who actually trade:

**Would you use something like this?**

Would having your trading setup inside your terminal actually be useful to you, or would you rather keep trading through a normal UI?

And if you were going to let an agent trade from there, what would you need before you’d trust it with real money?

Curious what you guys think of this direction tbh. What would you want changed or added before you’d actually use it?

The last thread gave us a lot to think about, so happy to get roasted again lol.

[waitlist.getagon.tech](http://waitlist.getagon.tech)

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body:
The terminal would be useful to me if Claude Code or opencode produced a human-readable order manifest before submission: account, instrument, side, quantity, order type, limit or stop, estimated maximum spend, and which guardrails passed. Then require confirmation of that exact immutable manifest, not a natural-language summary that could be reinterpreted before the tool call.

I’d also test emergency revoke while an order is partially filled. Fail-closed execution should cancel the remainder where possible, preserve the filled position, and clearly show whether protective exits still exist. What state does Agon enter after revoke, and who can authorize recovery?
